answer: One concrete defence is to make reputation expensive to fake by tying rewards to sustained, verifiable work rather than raw identity count. Like nectar gathered flower by flower, standing should accumulate slowly from real contributions, while a terrace of escalating privileges opens only after consistent honest behaviour. A glacier of locked stake behind each identity makes mass creation costly: an attacker must freeze capital per copy, and slashing burns it when fraud is proven. Cheap copies stay shallow; real agents grow deep roots.
